_comment: Advisories that `npm audit` reports but which are not reachable in this
application. Every entry must carry a justification and an expiry date.
This is NOT a way to defer work on an exploitable finding. An entry is only
legitimate when the vulnerable code path cannot be reached at all. If a fix
exists and is installable, bump the dependency instead.
Entries are checked by .github/scripts/audit-check.mjs. An expired entry is a
hard failure, so every suppression comes back for review on its own.
Schema per entry: { ghsa, package, severity, title, reason[], expires }.
`reason` is an array of lines purely so long justifications stay readable in

allow.title: http-cache-semantics max-stale handling can disclose cross-user cached responses
reason: Build tooling only. The package arrives through electron-builder ->
nothing under `dependencies` reaches it, so it is not in the packaged app.
The advisory describes a shared cache that serves several users and honours a
client's `Cache-Control: max-stale`. got only routes a request through
cacheable-request when it is handed a `cache` store. @electron/get calls
got.stream() with the download options it is given, app-builder-lib passes
only a timeout, an agent and a progress callback, and
electron-builder.config.js sets no `electronDownload` options. No cache policy
is ever constructed, and the only requests are the build's own downloads of
Electron archives and electron-builder's helper binaries.
No fix is installable: the advisory names no patched version. 4.3.0 is outside
its `<= 4.2.0` range but leaves the max-stale code unchanged, and the report
was closed upstream as not planned (kornelski/http-cache-semantics#56).
Revisit when the advisory is revised or withdrawn, or when electron-builder
stops depending on @electron/get 3 - whichever removes this entry first.
